findings.title: Invalid -ms-align-items property in align-items mixin
findings.body: The align-items() mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. There is no such CSS property in any IE version (IE10/11 use the standard `align-items` for modern layout, and `-ms-flex-align` for the old syntax, both of which are already emitted). This line is dead code that will be discarded by the CSS parser; it suggests a misunderstanding of the vendor prefix matrix and could mislead future maintainers into relying on it. It should be removed.

findings.title: float rules on children of new flex container are inert
findings.body: `.small-action` is now a flex container (via `@include flexbox()`), which makes `.topic-avatar { float: left; }` (line 270) and `button { float: right; }` (line 309) no-ops: per the flexbox spec, `float` is ignored on flex items. The layout now depends entirely on flex defaults (row, no wrapping, flex-start alignment), so the avatar will sit next to the description and the button will follow it — a visual change that may or may not be intended. Either the float declarations should be deleted as dead code, or explicit flex ordering/alignment (e.g. `margin-left: auto` on the button) should be added so the button is still pushed to the right edge; currently nothing in the diff guarantees the right-aligned button placement the old float provided.

findings.title: clear: both has no effect on a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` ends with `clear: both;`. With the element now converted to a flex container, `clear` still applies to the container itself as a block-level box, but since the container no longer has floated children (floats on flex items are ignored), the rule serves no purpose and, more importantly, the old clearfix-style guarantee that the small-action box contains its content is now handled differently. If the rule was meant to clear sibling floats (e.g. floated post streams above), it still works, but the comment-free combination of `clear: both` with floats and flexbox on the same element is contradictory and should be cleaned up to make the intended layout mechanism explicit.

findings.title: Header .title float removed but no flex sizing added; old-webkit-box fallback drops align-items
findings.body: `.d-header .contents` is now a flex container, and the `.title { float: left; }` rule was deleted. Two concerns: (1) In browsers that pick up the old `-webkit-box` display (older iOS Safari), the `align-items(center)` from the mixin will not apply because `-webkit-box` uses `-webkit-box-align` — that is emitted, but `center` is valid there so alignment is fine; however the `order(3)` on `.panel` is emitted as `-webkit-box-ordinal-group: 3`, which old WebKit honors, so ordering is fine — but `margin-left: auto` (the new right-pushing mechanism for `.panel`) is NOT supported as a flex-item auto-margin in the old -webkit-box model, so the panel will not be pushed to the right in those legacy browsers and the login/buttons will sit immediately next to the logo. (2) The old `float: left` on `.title` was the only thing constraining the title block; with flex and no explicit flex-grow, layout is unchanged for modern browsers, but the mixin emits five `display` values, meaning different browsers get different box models while only the modern properties (auto margins) are guaranteed to work in one of them. The legacy `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box`/`-ms-flexbox` fallbacks should either be dropped (Discourse does not target Firefox 21/IE10) or the layout must not depend on auto margins.

findings.title: order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only works if it is a direct flex child
findings.body: `@include order(2)` was added to `.extra-info-wrapper`. The `order` property only affects flex items, i.e. direct children of a flex container. This works only if `.extra-info-wrapper` is a direct child of `.d-header .contents`. The PR also removed the `margin-top: 5px` compensation for `.badge-wrapper.bullet` inside it while adding `line-height: 1.5` — if `.extra-info-wrapper` is not a direct flex child (or on pages where the header title area renders differently, e.g. topic pages vs. category pages), the `order` is silently ignored and the vertical spacing fix that was removed will not be replaced by flex centering, causing the category bullet badge to sit misaligned. Verify the element hierarchy across all header variants.
